For \(b=6\), \(a^6=64\) gives \(a=\pm 2\), so \((2,6)\) and \((-2,6)\) are solutions.

For negative exponents \(b=-n\) with \(n>0\),  
\[
a^{-n}=64 \implies a^n=\frac1{64},
\]
which is impossible for an integer \(a\). Thus no negative-exponent solutions.

Total solutions:
\[
(64,1),(8,2),(-8,2),(4,3),(2,6),(-2,6)
\]
so there are \(6\).

\boxed{6}
